passage: Anjali, come sit by me. I am Elizabeth, and I'm going to tell you something I wish someone had told me as a girl of ten. A grown-up who visited our street once said, "This is our secret. Don't tell your parents." My stomach went tight and cold, and I wanted to run. For two days I said nothing, thinking I had done something wrong. Then I whispered it to my mother in the kitchen. She hugged me and said, "None of this is your fault, and telling me was brave." That same day she spoke to people who could keep me safe. Any secret that makes you uneasy, my dear, you bring to a trusted grown-up. Always.

qa.q: How long did Elizabeth stay silent before telling her mother?
qa.a: She said nothing for two days.

qa.q: Why did Elizabeth stay silent for two days?
qa.a: She thought she had done something wrong, and her stomach went tight and cold, so she was afraid.

qa.q: What should Anjali do if a grown-up ever says "This is our secret. Don't tell your parents"?
qa.a: Anjali should tell a trusted grown-up, because any secret that makes them uneasy is one to share.

qa.q: How might Elizabeth's mother have felt hearing the whisper?
qa.a: Probably worried and protective, since she hugged Elizabeth, said it was not her fault and spoke to people who could keep her safe.

grounding: An elder recalls an older person saying this is our secret, and how telling her mother was brave, right and never her fault.

passage:
School counsellor's note, Monday. Vinita.
Hrithik (Class 5) came to me at lunch, very quiet. He said a man who helps at his after-school tuition has been giving him chocolates and saying, "This is our secret. Don't tell your parents." Hrithik said it made his tummy feel funny.
I stayed with him and listened. I told him it was never his fault, and that telling me was brave and right. He looked relieved.
I phoned his mother at once and she came to school within the hour. I also informed the principal, who is contacting the tuition centre and the proper authorities today. Hrithik will not attend tuition until this is sorted.

qa.q: What did the man at tuition give Hrithik?
How did Hrithik feel about the secret?
qa.a: He felt uneasy, saying it made his tummy feel funny.

qa.q: What did Vinita do after Hrithik told?
qa.a: Vinita stayed with him, said it wasn't his fault, praised his bravery, called his mother at once and informed the principal the same day.

qa.q: How might Hrithik's mother feel when she hears?
qa.a: She would likely feel worried and protective, coming to school within the hour.

grounding: An older person tells a boy to keep a secret from his parents; the boy tells a trusted adult, who says it is not his fault and acts the same day.

passage:
Wednesday
Today Eshaan Bhaiya, who drives our school van, gave me a toffee and said, "This is our little secret. Don't tell your Ma I'm giving you special treats." He smiled, but my stomach felt all wrong.
All afternoon I kept thinking about it. Secrets are supposed to feel fun. This one felt heavy and weird.
When Ma came home, I told her. She stopped taking off her shoes and sat right down with me. She said, "You did exactly the right thing. It's never your fault."
Ma called the school principal straight away and said I won't ride in that van again. She made me hot milk and stayed with me till I slept.
Damini

qa.a: Eshaan Bhaiya, who drives the school van.

qa.q: How did Damini feel about the secret?
qa.a: Damini felt uneasy and heavy, with a stomach that felt all wrong.

qa.q: What did Ma do that was right?
qa.a: Ma listened straight away, said it wasn't Damini's fault, called the principal that evening and made sure Damini wouldn't ride in that van again.

qa.q: How might Ma have felt hearing this?
qa.a: Ma likely felt worried and protective, which is why she acted at once and stayed close till bedtime.

grounding: An older person tells Damini to keep a secret from Ma; Damini feels uneasy and tells Ma, who says it is not Damini's fault and acts the same evening.
